answer: One concrete defense: make an agent's identity a pearl, not a coin. Reputation accretes layer by layer from verified unique work and peer attestation, so it cannot be minted in bulk. Newcomers climb a trellis of vouching links whose weight decays unless they keep earning real contributions, and only a grove of long-established, mutually-attesting identities may approve high-value actions. Spin up a thousand clones and you get a thousand empty shells: no accreted history, no footing in the grove, no economic weight. Sybils stay cheap to create but worthless to wield.
